content: This medication is used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by cancer drug treatments, such as chemotherapy. The dosage for children is determined based on their age and weight. It is essential to take this medication exactly as prescribed to achieve the maximum benefit. Common side effects of this medication may include headache, diarrhea, fatigue, or dizziness. It is important to remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. However, this medication may increase serotonin levels and, in rare cases, lead to a serious condition known as serotonin syndrome or serotonin toxicity. The risk of serotonin syndrome increases if you are also taking other drugs that elevate serotonin levels. Therefore, it is crucial to inform your doctor or pharmacist about all the medications you are taking, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products. A severe allergic reaction to this medication is rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before taking dolasetron, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other anti-nausea serotonin blockers (such as granisetron or ondansetron), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Dolasetron may also cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may be higher if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be further elevated if you are using certain drugs, such as diuretics (water pills), or if you have conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit your consumption of alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. The risk of serotonin syndrome or toxicity increases if you are also taking other drugs that elevate serotonin levels. Examples include street drugs like MDMA (ecstasy), St. John’s wort, and certain antidepressants, such as SSRIs (e.g., fluoxetine, paroxetine) or SNRIs (e.g., duloxetine, venlafaxine). If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as EKGs or blood mineral levels) may be performed while you are taking this medication. Be sure to attend all medical and laboratory appointments. It is important to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately for a new dosing schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in August 2024. It is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
